summary.text: Javier Valdez is a Democratic member of the Washington State Senate representing District 46, where he took office on January 9, 2023, after serving in the state House from 2017 to 2023, and he is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot seeking re-election against Sandra Stephens.

paragraphs.text: Javier Valdez was born in Moses Lake, Washington, and lives in Seattle.
He earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Washington and a master's degree in public administration from Baruch College, the City University of New York.

His career includes work for the City of Seattle, including leading Seattle City Light's women and minority business program and serving as a senior equity and inclusion advisor in the city's finance and administrative services department.
Valdez served on the executive board of the Washington State Democratic Party and chaired the 43rd and 46th District Democratic Party organizations.
He has been a board member of the Washington State Hispanic Chamber of Commerce and president of Hispanic Seafair and of AFSCME Council 2, Local 21-C.
Valdez represented District 46, Position 2, in the Washington House of Representatives from 2017 to 2023 and then moved to the Senate.
In 2023-2024 his Senate committees were Law & Justice; State Government, Tribal Relations & Elections, where he was vice chair; and Transportation.
